title: Constructible closed inverse image preserves finite scalar models, Tor bounds and adic completion
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow V$ be a closed immersion of qcqs schemes with quasi-compact complementary open [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. Put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ and use ordinary unbounded derived internal module categories [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, def-weil-size-convention]. Constructibility and Tor intervals mean [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. The exact inverse image $i^*$ sends finite constant scalar models to the same scalar models on the pulled-back pro-etale covers, sends constructible sheaves to constructible sheaves, and sends $D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(V,\Lambda)$ to $D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(Z,\Lambda)$ without enlarging any Tor interval. For every $K$ and every module sheaf $N$ on $Z$ the canonical tensor comparison and closed counit give
$$i^*(K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_V}i_*N)\cong i^*K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_Z}N.$$
Here $i_*N$ in the left side is the ordinary module sheaf in degree zero.
In addition fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $H/\mathbf Q_\ell$, $A=\mathcal O_H$ with its norm topology and uniformizer $\pi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and set $P_{n,T}=(A/\pi^n)_T$. For every derived $\pi$-complete $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{A_V})$, $i^*K$ is derived complete [sk-def-pe-derived-completion]. More precisely there is a canonical isomorphism
$$i^*R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_n(K\otimes^L_{A_V}P_{n,V})\cong R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_n(i^*K\otimes^L_{A_Z}P_{n,Z})$$
carrying $i^*$ of the completion unit to the completion unit of $i^*K$. On strict quotient towers its Roos representative is the product comparison in both coordinates of $\operatorname{Cone}(1-T)[-1]$, preserving the augmentation with zero second coordinate and the two-term resolutions $[A\xrightarrow{\pi^n}A]$. No boundedness of the complete $K$ is required.

proof.text: For the finite-model and Tor assertions work directly in internal modules: the coefficient isomorphism alpha_i makes ordinary inverse image exact, and exact-functor localization represents the unbounded derived pullback termwise. For the still postponed strict-completion assertion, retain the internal/section equivalence and its tensor comparison, the immersion-limit theorem, and their product-preservation argument.

The existing comparison CondensedRing.upperStarFromPointModComp identifies pullback of every point-module with the same point-module. Compose it with the module inverse-image composition isomorphisms around a commutative square. On the specified base-changed pro-etale cover this gives the identical modules P_a, preserving finite presentation without a matrix calculation. Apply the same comparison on the actual base-changed strata Scheme.Stratification.pullback; their finite local models give constructibility. All square comparisons are first established for abstract schemes and arrows, keeping concrete scheme pullback constructions out of coefficient reduction.

source.place: Constructible complexes paragraph; finite scalar matrix refinement; Stacks Tag 054I, morphisms.tex lemma-inverse-image-constructible

proof.text: Lift the proved abelian closed counit to internal modules through the module-adjunction counit formula: forgetting modules reflects isomorphisms. The scalar extension/restriction counit is invertible because the coefficient map is an isomorphism. Composition and right-adjoint isomorphism transport give invertibility of the actual internal-module counit. Combine this with the existing derived tensor comparison and the exact degree-zero comparison to obtain the specified tensor/counit isomorphism for the ordinary sheaf i_*N. Test the Tor interval on i_*N, preserve it by exact derived pullback, and transport along this isomorphism. The exact-functor homology comparison and preservation of stratified finite models also preserve bounded constructibility, proving D_ctf preservation with unchanged interval.

Countable products of module sheaves on both pro-etale sites are exact. Apply the exact-product-functor strict-limit theorem with $F=i^*$, using step 1 and the fixed small site universes. For every strict tower $M$, it gives $i^*R\varprojlim M\cong R\varprojlim i^*M$. This is the specified canonical comparison: on $\operatorname{Cone}(1-T)[-1]$ it is the canonical product comparison in both coordinates, and it carries every augmented map $(\gamma,0)$ to $(i^*\gamma,0)$. Its normalization is independent of resolutions.

source.place: Tag 0940, section-derived-limits, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok; normalized exact-product comparison as stated in lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit

proof.text: For the integral coefficient ring, use the exact resolution $[A_T\xrightarrow{\pi^n}A_T]\to P_{n,T}$. The scalar-matrix comparison identifies its inverse image with the same resolution on $Z$. The principal-reduction normalization computes $\operatorname{Res}_n(K\otimes^LP_{n,V})$ by the scalar cone of $\pi^n$ on any representing complex, with transition $(\pi,\mathrm{id})$ and augmentation the cone inclusion. Exact termwise $i^*$ preserves that cone, its scalar differential, transition and inclusion. The cited normalization identifies these with the actual quotient transition and derived scalar-extension unit on $Z$, not just isomorphic objects. Apply step 4 to this augmented strict tower. This is the asserted completion isomorphism and it carries $i^*$ of the completion unit to the actual completion unit of $i^*K$. This also proves the stated two-term-resolution and zero-second-coordinate normalization. All arguments apply to unbounded complexes.

proof.text: If $K$ is derived complete, its completion unit is invertible. Applying $i^*$ preserves its inverse; step 5 identifies the resulting map with the completion unit of $i^*K$. Hence that unit is invertible, which is precisely derived completeness.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q153-33ac64b70 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Statement-only item, split with no new nodes. The statement is identical to the base (checked against sibling Q153 base snapshots); the only stmt_dep added is sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom, which the statement's derived tensor requires. Source check: Stacks proetale 09BL (l.4852), 09AA (l.4945) and 099M (l.4305) say what the item cites them for. No SGA. Step 1: the immersion-limit lemma applies with coefficient map c = alpha_i, which lem-sfb-alpha-iso makes an isomorphism; the internal/sectionwise equivalences are exact. Step 2: constructible preimage, immersion base change, fpqc and weakly-etale base change, and the scalar-matrix lemma give the same finitely presented models on Z_a, which is exactly the definition in sk-def-sfb-constructible. Step 3: the derived-pullback tensor iso (any morphism, unbounded complexes) plus the ringed closed counit for i_*N in degree 0 give the tensor iso. The Tor test in the definition runs over all module sheaves N, so the interval is preserved. Step 4: every hypothesis of lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit holds (exact countable products on both sites, exact product-preserving F). Step 5: the principal-reduction normalization has a_n = pi^{n+1}, covering every level n >= 1; transition (pi,id) and the cone inclusion are preserved strictly by termwise i^*, so the units correspond. Step 6 is elementary. Small cases (i = id, empty Z, K = 0) behave correctly. lem-sfb-pullback-constant-model-constructible covers clause 2 only for admissible rings and lem-sf-immersion-completed-pullback-comparison works over a different ring (lim A_n), so neither duplicates the item. The declared tool_uses are accepted. Batch-5 flag: lem-trf-localization-essentially-surjective is a mathlib-status category-theory fact (localizations are essentially surjective) and derived-pullback monoidality is general, so neither is part of the trace-formula or Poincare-duality proofs; I accepted the citation.
